papers.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
papers.abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.

papers.title: A smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain with incomplete Kobayashi distance
papers.abstract: We construct a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\C^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary which is not Kobayashi complete. The domain has a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function, and its Carath\'eodory distance is also incomplete. We then prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain with $C^\infty$ boundary of finite D'Angelo type is Kobayashi complete. Consequently, every bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary is Kobayashi complete. We also obtain quantitative lower estimates for the Kobayashi--Royden metric and the Kobayashi distance in the finite-type case.

papers.title: On Euler's abelian relation of the web induced by the forgetful maps on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M_{0,n+3}}$: the case when $n$ is even
papers.abstract: In a previous paper ${\bf [P1]}$, for every $n\geq 2$, we studied the curvilinear web $\boldsymbol{\mathcal W}_{0,n+3}$ on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}$, defined by the $n+3$ forgetful maps $ \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}\rightarrow \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+2}$, with particular emphasis on its abelian relations. In particular, when $n$ is even, we conjectured an explicit formula for its Euler abelian relation. This relation is constructed \`a la Gelfand-MacPherson from an invariant differential form representing the appropriate power of the Euler class of the tautological bundle of the Grassmannian manifold $G_2^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathbf R^{n+3})$ of oriented $2$-planes in $\mathbf R^{n+3}$. In this note, we obtain an explicit antisymmetrized formula for Euler's abelian relation for every even $n\geq 2$, and prove that it coincides, up to the explicit factor $-(n+1)(n+2)/2$, with the formula conjectured in ${\bf [P1]}$, which is therefore established for all even $n$.

papers.title: On the automorphisms of Pick bodies
papers.abstract: We determine the biholomorphic automorphisms of the Pick body associated with finitely many distinct points in a Carath\'eodory hyperbolic domain. Every automorphism is the composition of a common disc automorphism applied to all coordinates and a coordinate permutation preserving the Pick body. The proof uses the quotient Banach algebra of interpolation data, its generalized von Neumann inequality, and the fact that its symmetric part consists precisely of the constant vectors. For nodes in a polydisc, we introduce minimal effective coordinate tuples and identify the admissible permutations with the automorphisms of a lower-dimensional polydisc that preserve the projected node set. This yields a direct-product description of the automorphism group, with one factor equal to the automorphism group of the disc and the other finite. We also give the resulting descriptions for nodes in the disc and the bidisc.

papers.title: Rigidity of Pseudoconvex Neighborhoods and Ohsawa--Takegoshi Extension
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a holomorphic section of a holomorphic submersion with one-dimensional fibers over a connected compact complex manifold. Assuming that its normal bundle is unitary flat, we prove that $Y$ admits a fundamental system of locally pseudoconvex neighborhoods if and only if it admits a holomorphic tubular neighborhood. The proof uses the sharp Ohsawa--Takegoshi extension theorem. As an application, we rule out such neighborhood systems in Ueda's example of class $(\gamma)$.

papers.title: On evaluation of polynomial coefficients
papers.abstract: The evaluation of polynomial coefficients is an old mathematical problem, which is still actively investigated by many authors. The paper strengthens the known results in this direction and provides a complete solution for the case when the space $P_n$ of polynomials is equipped with Hilbert's norm. Our approach involves the intrinsic features of univalent functions and of Teichmuller spaces.

papers.title: Principle of generating critical points of rational functions and Gauss-Fourier conjecture for second-kind zeros
papers.abstract: The precise origin of critical points in rational functions remains a longstanding open problem. This paper elucidates the mechanism underlying critical point generation in rational functions. For over two centuries, a conjecture attributed to Gauss and Fourier has remained unresolved: every real zero of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ is associated with a pair of non-real zeros of the real polynomial $p(s)$. The real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ that are multiple real zeros of $p^{'}(s)$ are termed second-kind zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. By developing the root locus method, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the emergence of second-kind zeros: a second-kind zero $M$ arises if and only if at least two root loci of $2q\pi$ or $2q\pi+\pi$ degree, emitted from at least one pair of non-real conjugate zeros of $p(s)$ (in the extended complex plane, excluding the real axis), directly intersect another root locus at $M$ on the real axis. Our results resolve one conjecture of the Gauss-Fourier conjectures and reveal the fundamental mechanism by which critical points of rational functions are generated.

papers.title: On complete Ricci--flat K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We study complete noncompact Ricci-flat K\"ahler manifolds. In the case of Euclidean volume growth, we prove that the underlying complex manifold is naturally quasi-projective and that the asymptotic cone is unique. Moreover, we establish no semistability at infinity and prove convergence to the asymptotic cone at a polynomial rate. In the case of sub-Euclidean volume growth, we construct complete Ricci-flat K\"ahler threefolds with bounded sectional curvature and finite topological type that admit no K\"ahler compactification.

papers.title: Irregular Gabor Frames for the Poisson Kernel
papers.abstract: Consider the semi-regular system of time-frequency shifts of the Poisson kernel $g(t) = {{1} \over {t^2+w^2}}$ $$\G(g, M \times \alpha \Z) = \left\{ e^{2\pi i \lambda t } g(t-n) \colon (\lambda, n) \in M \times \alpha\Z \right\}$$ where $M \subset \R$. We obtain {\it a criterion} for $\G(g, M \times \alpha \Z)$ to form a frame in $L^2(\R)$ for an {\it arbitrary} set $M$ of finite upper density. It turned out that the lower density alone does not determine the frame property, even when $M$ is uniformly discrete.

papers.title: On the complement of nef divisors on projective manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X'$ be a complex projective manifold, $\dim X'>1$, $Z$ a connected analytic subset of codimension one which is the support of a nef effective Cartier divisor $D$ on $X'$, $X:=X'\setminus Z$. Let $\kappa(D)$ be the Iitaka dimension of $D$. We prove that $X$ is not Hartogs if and only if $D$ is abundant and $\kappa(D)=1$. In particular, $X$ is not Hartogs if and only if $X$ is a proper fibration over an affine curve.

papers.title: Obstructions to the ampleness of invariant jet differentials on complete intersections
papers.abstract: We introduce the analogue, for invariant jet differentials, of the principal symbol of a differential operator: the component of maximal degree in the highest derivative. The top symbol identifies a canonical quotient bundle of the Demailly--Semple bundle $E_{k,m}T^*_X$, with values in jet differentials of lower order, and together with the Br\"uckmann--Rackwitz vanishing theorem it gives a non-ampleness criterion for $E_{k,m}T^*_Z$ on complete intersections $Z\subset\PP^N$. On the Demailly--Semple tower the top symbol is the restriction to a thickening of the vertical divisor, inside the singular jets. The criterion applies in orders $3$ and $4$: $E_{3,5q}T^*_X$ is not ample on any smooth hypersurface $X\subset\PP^4$, and $E_{4,m}T^*_X$ is not ample for $m\ge7$ with $m\equiv0,1,2\pmod 7$ on any smooth hypersurface $X\subset\PP^5$ of degree at least $2$. This contradicts the Diverio--Trapani conjecture at its own threshold.

papers.title: Complex zero strip decreasing operators
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the effect of linear differential operators coming from the Laguerre-Polya class that act on functions in the extended Laguerre-Polya class with zeros in a horizontal strip in the complex plane. These operator decrease the size of the strip containing the zeros.

papers.title: Subclass of bi-univalent function associated to Chebyshev polynomial
papers.abstract: The Chebyshev polynomials are utilized in this study to define the subclass of the bi-univalent function. Also, Chebyshev polynomial bounds and Fekete-Szego inequalities for functions defined in the classes are established.

papers.title: A Note on Zoll Manifolds with Entire Grauert Tubes
papers.abstract: We compute several algebraic indices of the algebraization of the tangent bundle of a Zoll manifold that admits an entire Grauert tube. As an application, we prove that any Zoll manifold of type $\mathbb{HP}^2$ with an entire Grauert tube is isometric to the canonical $\mathbb{HP}^2$.

papers.title: Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions and Fujii-Seo Determinants in Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: A maximal plurisubharmonic function on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space can have an injective, noncompact Levi operator at every point. This raises the question of what replaces the finite-dimensional determinant criterion for maximality. We prove that a twice continuously differentiable plurisubharmonic function is maximal if its Levi operator is compact at every point, without any boundedness assumption on the function. Using the normalized determinants of Fujii and Seo, we also characterize local maximality by the condition that the infimum of the spectrum of the Levi operator is zero. The same condition characterizes maximality when the function is bounded on the closure of every bounded open set whose closure lies in the domain. The compactness result follows from a more general spectral criterion. Its proof combines a bounded transformation with the smooth variational principle of Borwein and Preiss to establish comparison on bounded open sets whose closures need not be compact.

papers.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
papers.abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.

papers.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbf R^n$ be a set of dimension $2$ with an isolated singular point $0$, such that $E-\{0\}$ is an orientable $\mathcal C^2$ submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$ of dimension $2$, and hence a Riemann surface with the conformal structure induced by the ambient metric. We study the extension of its conformal structure across $0$, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. Denoting by $S(0,r)$ the sphere of radius $r$ centred at $0$, we call the singularity $0$ $\mathit{M\text{-}regular}$ if (i) the pair $(E-\{0\},\{0\})$ satisfies a Whitney condition (the radial direction becomes asymptotically tangent to $E-\{0\}$ at $0$) and (ii) the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ is bounded above by a linear function of $r$ for small $r$ ($\mathit{metric\ decay}$). The main result (1989) is that an $M$-regular singularity is $\mathit{conformally\ point\text{-}like}$, that is, a punctured neighbourhood of $0$ in $E$ is conformal to the punctured unit disc $\Delta^*$, so that the conformal structure extends across $0$. The proof uses the modulus of rings (extremal length), which generalizes the classical planar technique to $2$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Two classes of surfaces are shown to be conformally point-like: all surfaces of revolution generated by a single $C^1$ curve, and orientable subanalytic sets of dimension $2$ with isolated singularities, for which $M$-regularity is proven directly from Hironaka's structure theory. In this case the metric decay condition follows from a direct estimate of the volume of the slices $S(0,r)\cap E$ (Lemma 7.5), based on Hironaka's Whitney theorem and Stasica's decomposition into $L$-analytic pieces. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\mathit{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses defining $M$-regularity are independent.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant and admissible univalent Blaschke pairs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of polynomials $P$ of degree at least $2$ with $P(0)=0$, $P'(0)=1$, let $S(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P(c)/c|$ and let $\mathcal{M}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}S(P)$ be Smale's mean value constant. Smale proved that $\mathcal{M}\le4$, observed that $\mathbb{M}\ge 1$, and asked whether $\mathcal{M}=1$. We show that $\mathcal{M}$ coincides with $$ \mathcal{B}=\sup\frac1{B(0)}, $$ the supremum running over pairs $(W,B)$ in which $W$ is a normalised univalent map of the standard unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $B$ is a finite Blaschke product with $B(0)>0$ such that $WB$ is locally univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Smale's question is therefore a problem in univalent function theory. We also introduce the degree-restricted constants $\mathcal{B}_d$ for $B$ with $\mathrm{deg} B \le d$ and show that $$1.1018586788\ldots=\sqrt{\frac{8081}{6656}} \le \mathcal{B}_1 < \sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}=1.1832159566\ldots$$ This implies that $\mathcal{M}>1.1018$ and we also show that there are polynomials of arbitrarily large degree with $S(P)>1.1018$. The polynomial construction behind these results also settles Problems 1A and 1B of Smale's 1981 paper. For $P\in\mathcal P$ and an integer $k\ge2$ let $S_k(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P^{(k)}(0)/k!|^{1/(k-1)}|P(c)|$. Smale proved, by L\"owner's coefficient estimate for inverses of univalent functions, that $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}S_k(P)\le C_k^{1/(k-1)}<4$, where $C_k$ is the $k$-th Catalan number and he asked whether the constant $4$ (Problem 1A), or the constant $2=C_2$ for $k=2$ (Problem 1B), can be reduced. We prove that $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}S_k(P)=C_k^{1/(k-1)}$ for every $k\ge2$. Hence the constants $4$ and $2$ cannot be reduced and the answers to both problems are negative.
